Help

        

          
          

            

            

              
Open file and drag and drop work the same way. A Midihub backup (.mhd) opens the whole setup. For a preset (.mhp), check the slots to fill or use Select all for all eight. Check Create a new setup to place those copies in a fresh setup. Piper JSON opens according to whether it contains a preset or a setup.

              
Use File → Rename file to change the name shown in the browser tab and used for downloads. Piper asks for a name the first time you download an untitled document.

              
When loading a preset into the open setup, Port names appears if the source and destination defaults would display different names. One Undo restores all replaced slots.

              
    
                
  • Download preset saves the selected preset as .mhp. If it uses a custom tuning, that tuning must be available on the receiving device.
    • 
                
  • Download everything saves all eight presets, device settings, and tuning tables from an open setup.
    • 
                
  • Download JSON saves all eight presets, device settings and shared tunings with instructions for an AI agent. Give the file to your agent with the changes you want, then open the returned JSON in Piper to try it.
    • 
              

            

          

          

            

            

              
New setup creates eight empty slots. When you start a setup from a preset, it supplies the selected slots and port names. Other device settings use Piper’s defaults and shared tunings start empty. File → Init current preset clears the selected slot.

              
In Presets → Copy preset, choose a source and destination slot in the open setup. Choose Init as the source to clear the destination. Undo restores its previous contents.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Drag a pipe from Pipes onto a pipeline. To start a new pipeline, drop an input on empty map space. Click a pipe to edit its parameters or MIDI mappings.

              
In Virtual routing, select a pipeline number to jump to the pipe connected to that virtual port. To save the map’s displayed order, open Presets → Pipeline order and choose Apply pipeline order.

              
Press Delete to remove the selected pipe. On a pipeline’s starting input, this removes the whole pipeline. Undo restores it.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Choose the input tab that feeds your pipeline, then Add source. A Notes source plays a chord or an arpeggio. Turn on Hold to sustain the chord or repeat the arpeggio until you stop. Start input plays one input’s configured sources and Start all plays across inputs.

              
To try a controller mapping, add an Expression pedal, match its channel and CC to the mapping, and move the floating slider. Use MIDI message to send a single event.

              
If a note keeps sounding after you stop playback, use MIDI Panic beside the MIDI Studio controls to silence Piper and its selected hardware outputs.

              
Built-in instruments use WebAudioTinySynth under Apache 2.0.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Choose Connect to Midihub to access the device over USB. If Midihub Editor is using the port, disconnect it in the Editor.

              
Import preset from Midihub lets you choose one saved hardware slot, then check the slots to fill in the open setup or a new one. Export preset to Midihub writes the selected Piper preset to the hardware slot you choose and makes it active.

              
Import everything from Midihub opens all eight slots, device settings and shared tunings. Export everything to Midihub previews which slots and shared settings will change and which preset will be active afterward. Confirming writes the full setup. Piper reads it back to verify the result. To restore an unreadable slot, open a known-good copy and export it to the affected slot.

              
To play from a controller, add a MIDI input source in MIDI Studio, allow MIDI access in your browser, and choose your device.

              
To hear the result on a synth, select its port under Destination for notes or a hardware input, or MIDI out for messages and pedals. If the ports aren’t listed yet, choose Find MIDI outputs…. The synth receives events that reach an output in your preset.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Open MIDI activity to see which messages entered a pipeline, reached an output, or were dropped. For one pipe’s messages, click it on the map and open Pipe activity.

              
Log messages filters the event list and its clipboard copy. Animated selects which events light up connections on the map. Enable clock ticks in either filter when you want to trace timing.

            

          

          

            

            

              
Drag empty map space to pan. Scroll to zoom at the pointer. Drag a panel’s dotted grip to dock it in a corner or reorder it. Double-click its width grip to restore its default width.

              
With the dotted grip focused, use Left or Right to change sides, Shift+Up or Shift+Down to change corners vertically, and Up or Down to reorder. Home restores the original position.
